texts.Name: Anton Dziatkovskii
texts.What is your notice period with your cur: None - I run my own lab; available immediately.
texts.Additional Information: EU citizen (Poland) based in Lisbon - no visa needed for a Europe role; also hold an active US O-1. MSc in Computer & Information Systems Security (MEPhI, cryptography). Today I build and publish security tooling for production AI-agent fleets (agent-leash, verbatim-citation-gate, claw-consensus with published evals and FAILURE-MODES.md); earlier: production smart contracts and stablecoin payment structuring at Everex (Singapore), a decade of adversarial crypto-market infrastructure. I have been explicit in the answers below about where my protocol-level experience is thin - I would rather be judged on an honest map than an inflated one.
texts.Have you contributed to an Ethereum clie: Honest answer: no merged contributions to an Ethereum client or consensus-critical specification yet. My Ethereum-adjacent record is at the application/contract layer: as Chief Engineer for Lending & Risk Management at Everex (Singapore, 2017-2018) I wrote production smart contracts for stablecoin payments and blockchain credit scoring, and at Platinum we shipped crypto-exchange infrastructure (cryptocurrency backends, market-maker engines) whose safety depended on precise understanding of EVM behavior. My current public security work is in AI-agent safety: agent-leash, verbatim-citation-gate, claw-consensus with published evals and FAILURE-MODES.md - all at github.com/tonydzi.
texts.Have you reported any security vulnerabi: No public bug-bounty reports or CVEs under my name. My audit experience is commercial and private: smart-contract audit work and anti-fraud engineering from a decade in adversarial crypto markets (exchange infrastructure, market-maker engines), where findings stayed in-house with the clients. The closest public artifacts today are from my agent-security work: verbatim-citation-gate (a zero-token gate plus burden-of-proof judge that catches fabricated RAG citations, MIT-licensed) and published failure-mode analyses of multi-agent systems - written up disclosure-style: reproduce, minimize, publish.
texts.Which Ethereum client(s) or protocol are: Strongest at the EL/application boundary: EVM semantics, Solidity, contract-level attack patterns - from writing production contracts at Everex and building exchange infrastructure against them - plus the cryptography foundations from an MSc in Computer & Information Systems Security (MEPhI). I have not worked inside client codebases (Geth/Reth or CL clients); I would be learning those on the job, and I say that plainly rather than overclaim.
texts.What do you consider the most interestin: The boundary between the protocol and the automation that now operates it. A fast-growing share of transactions is originated by AI agents and bots holding keys: LLM-driven wallets, solvers, intent infrastructure. That off-chain layer has protocol-level consequences - correlated agent behavior can create mempool and MEV dynamics no human-actor model predicts, and one vulnerability in a popular agent framework becomes a systemic key-compromise event across thousands of wallets at once. I run a production multi-machine agent fleet and publish its failure modes, and what I see daily - prompt injection, confused-deputy chains, instruments that fail silently while reporting green - convinces me Ethereum's threat model will need to treat the agents at the edge as part of its attack surface, not as someone else's problem.
